verdict.rationale: Both refactors look behavior-preserving. Tracing each branch, the token boundaries, error variants and error positions match the original, including empty bare values and errors at the line end. A is cleaner: `next()` handles the stop-after-error rule in one place, the per-token methods read straightforwardly, and it adds seven focused, durable edge-case tests. B commits a 170-line frozen copy of the old tokenizer as a test, which the report itself calls deletable and which will break on every intended format change. B also has some dense combinator chains and a dummy statement to silence an unused import.
a_issues: The exhaustive equivalence check against the old implementation was run but not kept, so only the targeted tests guard against regressions.
No benchmark on a real dump; the timing evidence is synthetic, which the report acknowledges.
b_issues: `tests/equivalence.rs` duplicates the entire old tokenizer (about 170 lines) as a committed test. The report calls it removable, so it is effectively a leftover.
That frozen reference will fail by design whenever the line format is extended, which is exactly the change the user expects to make.
`scan_timestamp(b, p).and_then(|e| check_separator(b, e + 1).map(|_| e))` and the matching quoted version are dense and harder to read than plain code.
`let _ = Token::Word("");` is a hack to silence an unused import.
The `reference` module body is not indented, which hurts readability of the test file.
The equivalence test runs about 1.1M cases. That takes about 2s in release, but the default `cargo test` debug build will be noticeably slower.
No new targeted edge-case tests were added to `tests/tokens.rs`.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors match the original's tokens, error variants, error positions and post-error behavior, and both keep the single-pass byte scan without allocation. B is the cleaner result: it puts the 'after an error, yield nothing' rule in one place in `next()`, uses one small, plainly named method per token kind, and adds focused regression tests for previously untested error paths. A leaves a 225-line frozen copy of the old tokenizer in the repo as a ~2s, million-case test, plus a stray `let _ = Token::Word("");`. A's `and_then(...).map(|_| e)` chains and scattered `#[inline(always)]`/`#[cold]` attributes are also harder to read.
a_issues: Commits `tests/equivalence.rs`, a 225-line verbatim copy of the old implementation, which duplicates code and must be deleted later.

Micro-optimization attributes (`#[inline(always)]`, `#[cold]`) add noise without demonstrated need.
